items.title: Travel VC Funding Fell for the Second Straight Quarter, Rounds for AI Companies Cut in Half
items.summary: Travel's next dollar is shifting. Funding rounds steadily dropped quarter over quarter in 2026 while incumbents made targeted acquisitions. Though it's too early to say whether this is a long-term market movement, it's a clear sign of the times.

items.title: PS’s CEO on Running the Private Terminal and the Power of Restraint
items.summary: PS has built one of the more defensible businesses in premium travel on a 90-minute window and nearly a decade of regulatory groundwork. For hotels, lounges, and clubs chasing the same customer, the lesson is that protecting a guest's attention can be worth more than monetiz

items.title: UAE Hotels Lean On Short-Haul Markets To Drive Recovery
items.summary: Luxury hotels that rely on long-haul, high spending guests have been hit by Middle East unrest while their budget and midscale counterparts have fared better with a broader mix of arrivals.

items.title: Who Owns a Traveler’s Connectivity? Airlines, Hotels, and Platforms Share the Responsibility
items.summary: Travelers do not separate a connectivity failure from the rest of their trip. Airlines, hotels, platforms, and connectivity providers must build reliable access into the journey before AI raises the stakes.

items.title: They Just Booked the Hotel Room — But They’re Already Looking for a Better Deal
items.summary: With 41% of travelers still price-checking after they book, the hotel and flight reservations are now only one part of a longer, more dynamic  — and more provisional —  process.

items.title: Southeast Asia’s Haze Lands on Malaysia’s Already Flat Tourism Year
items.summary: Malaysia’s 47 million target was out of reach before the haze arrived; the year-end damage now depends on whether travelers rule out more than the worst-hit areas.

items.title: Death Toll From Europe’s Extreme Summer Heat Estimated At More Than 50,000
items.summary: The toll of extreme heat is mounting. Europe’s tourism industry, on a continent largely resistant to air conditioning, must figure out how to adapt — as a matter of safety, not just comfort.
